title: Dengue Fever
subtitle: A mosquito-borne viral disease caused by any of four dengue viruses (DENV 1-4), transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.

sections.title: Symptoms
sections.intro: Dengue fever causes a severe flu-like illness that can occasionally develop into potentially lethal complications called severe dengue. Symptoms typically appear 4, 10 days after a mosquito bite.
items: Sudden high fever, 40°C (104°F)
Severe headache, especially behind the eyes
Severe joint and muscle pains (breakbone fever)
Nausea and vomiting
Skin rash appearing 2, 5 days after onset
Mild bleeding (nose bleed, gum bleed, easy bruising)

sections.title: Causes
sections.intro: Dengue is caused by the dengue virus (DENV), of which there are four distinct serotypes. Infection with one serotype provides immunity only to that type, you can be infected up to four times.
items: DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, DENV-4, four serotypes of dengue virus
Transmitted primarily by female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes
Aedes albopictus (tiger mosquito) is a secondary vector
Mosquitoes breed in stagnant water in and around homes

sections.title: Prevention
items: Eliminate standing water, flower pots, buckets, tyres
Use mosquito repellent on exposed skin (DEET-based)
Wear long-sleeved clothing in high risk areas
Use mosquito nets, especially during daytime bites
Install window and door screens
Community-level mosquito control programs

sections.title: Treatment
items: No specific antiviral treatment for dengue
Paracetamol for fever, avoid aspirin and ibuprofen (increase bleeding risk)
Rest and drink plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration
Monitor platelet count, hospitalize if count drops sharply
IV fluid replacement for severe dengue
Blood transfusion in cases of severe bleeding

facts: Up to 20% untreated; under 1% with proper care
